1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Scene reader
24|
25|One static route per scene (`app/leer/[sceneId]`, `dynamicParams`
26|false); `/` redirects to the first scene. The layout mounts the music
27|container once and passes slim metadata for all scenes: id, chapter,
28|and emotion triple only. Each scene page builds its view with
29|`buildSceneView` and ships only that scene's text, its chapter title,
30|and neighbor ids. Sub-pages come from `paginateScene` (250 words, split
31|at paragraph boundaries). The pager moves sub-pages in client state and
32|pushes routes with `router.push`, never `<Link>`; going back lands on
33|the previous scene's last sub-page through a one-shot client flag, never
34|a URL param, so prerendered pages stay static. The client never
35|receives other scenes' text, titles, or summaries.
36|
37|## Music library
38|
39|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 3, fetched
40|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
41|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
42|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so. A version 2
43|manifest migrates inline to one implicit `default` soundtrack of style
44|`orchestral`.
45|
46|`MusicManifest = { version, styles, soundtracks, tracks, playlists }`.
47|`StyleInfo = { id, name }` where `id` is a lowercase slug and `name` is
48|the display name. `Soundtrack = { id, name, style }` plus
49|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,
50|intensity, tempo, durationSec, soundtrack, style }` plus optional
51|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
52|loop), `endSec` (default the media end, where the track stops or loops),
53|`gainDb` (default 0, a loudness trim in dB, in -24..12),
54|`loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
55|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
56|`sourceUrl` (https only). `durationSec` is the playable length: the
57|segment end (or the file end) minus `startSec`. `startSec` and `endSec`
58|are absolute media times with `startSec < endSec`; `endSec` stays within
59|`startSec + durationSec`. The player scales volume by the track gain and
60|ends or loops at `effectiveEnd`, the earlier of `endSec` and the loaded
61|media end. `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
62|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
63|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
64|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
65|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
66|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
67|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
68|a negative `startSec`, a bad `gainDb` or `endSec`, unknown `source`
69|values, a non-boolean
70|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
71|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. Unknown fields stay
72|ignored. A soundtrack with no
73|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
74|fails loudly in dev. Remote audio lives on one Blob store, so
75|`media-src` in `next.config.ts` lists exactly
76|`https://3vuhzq2wmortnuxj.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`. Build the
77|manifest with `npm run build:music data/music/labels.json
78|data/music/library.json --out public/music/manifest.json`, which runs
79|`pipeline/labels-to-manifest.ts` and validates the result before
80|writing.
81|
82|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
83|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
84|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
85|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
86|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
87|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
88|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
89|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
90|
91|## Selection
92|
93|`MusicSelection = { style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick.
94|There is one mode only. Every scheduled select ranges over all tracks in
95|the current style and draws among the tracks with the scene emotion (or
96|the best same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within
97|`randomTolerance` (0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when
98|it is eligible, and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. The style is
99|the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The default style is
100|the first listed style with tracks; a stored style with tracks wins. The
101|session persists `{ style }` in localStorage under `lectoria.music.v1`.
102|Old values with `mode` or `soundtrackId` load by `style` alone and
103|ignore unknown fields. A stored style with no tracks falls back to the
104|default. Storage exceptions never break playback. Dwell and min-track
105|rules hold. The core never calls `Math.random`; the reader injects it
106|and tests pass a seeded stub.
107|
108|## Next track and style change
109|
110|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order across the whole
111|style, wrapping and skipping the current, then the best same-style track
112|overall when the emotion is missing. A null scene cycles the style set
113|in id order. One track or none gives null.
114|
115|`requestStyleChange` picks the best match for the scene in the new style
116|by score. It never crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once
117|with the normal crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
118|mix toggle and no soundtrack-change button.
119|
120|## Playlist mode
121|
122|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
123|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
124|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
125|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
126|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
127|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
128|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
129|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
130|restored selection. The playlist is never persisted, so a reload returns
131|to emotion mode. The style selector stays disabled while it is on, and
132|the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
133|
134|## Similarity and config
135|
136|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
137|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
138|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
139|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
140|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
141|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
142|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
143|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
144|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
145|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
146|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
147|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
148|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
149|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
150|and overrides are unchanged.
151|
152|## Selection scheduler
153|
154|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
155|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
156|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
157|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
158|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
159|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
160|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
161|with the scene it belongs to.
162|
163|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
164|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
165|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
166|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
167|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
168|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
169|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
170|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
171|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
172|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
173|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
174|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
175|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
176|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
177|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
178|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
179|skip override.
180|
181|## Player
182|
183|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
184|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
185|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
186|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
187|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
188|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
189|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
190|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
191|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
192|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
193|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
194|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
195|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
196|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
197|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
198|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
199|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
200|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
201|
202|The bar is one contained row (reader column width, centered with
203|margins): Previous, Play/Pause, Next, the now-playing line
204|(flexible, truncated with an ellipsis), a speaker-icon volume slider with
205|`aria-label` `Volume`, a style selector with `aria-label`
206|`Orchestra / Piano` and no visible label text listing only styles that
207|have tracks (hidden while fewer than two qualify), then
208|`Just play Chopin`. The three transport buttons and the source icon link
209|are icon-only inline SVGs (`currentColor`, 32 px hit area), quiet
210|and neutral, Meta blue on hover and focus-visible, each with `aria-label`
211|and `title` (the source link reads `Source`). Previous walks the session
212|history and restarts the current track with no history, including the
213|current playlist piece in playlist mode; Next cycles same-emotion tracks
214|in the style.
215|A `Just play Chopin` toggle appears only when
216|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; its text comes from the
217|playlist label, it carries `aria-pressed`, and it shows the Meta blue
218|accent while pressed. The now-playing line shows `display title · composer
219|· source`: `displayTitle` drops quoted nicknames, key phrases, and
220|opus/catalogue suffixes from the track title, and the source is the
221|artist plus ` / <platform>` when the attribution names Musopen or
222|Jamendo and the artist does not already say it, dropped when it would
223|repeat the performer. The full manifest title plus the license and full
224|attribution sits in the `title` tooltip. A source icon link stays compact
225|when the manifest provides one. On manifest failure the reader still renders and
226|the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms.
227|Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and
228|keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine, transport, and
229|bar layout; `app/player-controls.tsx` holds the style selector and the
230|playlist toggle; `app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage helper.
231|`core/music-credit.ts` builds the line as a pure function with tests,
232|including the pure `displayTitle`.
233|`core/music-history.ts` is the bounded history stack and
234|`requestManualTrack` in `core/music-schedule.ts` holds a manual pick.
235|
236|## Image api
237|
238|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
239|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
240|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
241|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
242|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
243|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic English message.
244|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Illustrate
245|scene" uses the scene id from the route.
246|
247|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
248|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
249|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
250|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
251|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
252|friendly English message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
253|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
254|
255|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
256|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
257|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
258|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
259|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
260|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
261|and backfills the index.
262|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
263|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
264|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
265|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
266|quota and budget and release the lock.
267|
268|## Chat api
269|
270|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
271|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
272|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
273|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
274|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
275|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
276|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
277|
278|## Quotas and budget
279|
280|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
281|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
282|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
283|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
284|the client, details stay in server logs.

48|the display name. `Soundtrack = { id, name, style }` plus
49|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,
50|intensity, tempo, durationSec, soundtrack, style }` plus optional
51|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
52|loop), `endSec` (default the media end, where the track stops or loops),
53|`gainDb` (default 0, a loudness trim in dB, in -24..12),

57|segment end (or the file end) minus `startSec`. `startSec` and `endSec`
58|are absolute media times with `startSec < endSec`; `endSec` stays within
59|`startSec + durationSec`. The player scales volume by the track gain and
60|ends or loops at `effectiveEnd`, the earlier of `endSec` and the loaded
61|media end. `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
62|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
63|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
64|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
65|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
66|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
67|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
68|a negative `startSec`, a bad `gainDb` or `endSec`, unknown `source`
69|values, a non-boolean
70|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
71|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. Unknown fields stay
72|ignored. A soundtrack with no
73|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
74|fails loudly in dev. Remote audio lives on one Blob store, so
75|`media-src` in `next.config.ts` lists exactly
76|`https://3vuhzq2wmortnuxj.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`. Build the
77|manifest with `npm run build:music data/music/labels.json
78|data/music/library.json --out public/music/manifest.json`, which runs
79|`pipeline/labels-to-manifest.ts` and validates the result before
80|writing.
81|
82|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
83|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
84|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
85|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
86|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
87|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
88|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
89|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
90|
91|## Selection
92|
93|`MusicSelection = { style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick.
94|There is one mode only. Every scheduled select ranges over all tracks in
95|the current style and draws among the tracks with the scene emotion (or
96|the best same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within
97|`randomTolerance` (0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when
98|it is eligible, and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. The style is
99|the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The default style is
100|the first listed style with tracks; a stored style with tracks wins. The
101|session persists `{ style }` in localStorage under `lectoria.music.v1`.
102|Old values with `mode` or `soundtrackId` load by `style` alone and
103|ignore unknown fields. A stored style with no tracks falls back to the
104|default. Storage exceptions never break playback. Dwell and min-track
105|rules hold. The core never calls `Math.random`; the reader injects it
106|and tests pass a seeded stub.
107|
108|## Next track and style change
109|
110|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order across the whole
111|style, wrapping and skipping the current, then the best same-style track
112|overall when the emotion is missing. A null scene cycles the style set
113|in id order. One track or none gives null.
114|
115|`requestStyleChange` picks the best match for the scene in the new style
116|by score. It never crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once
117|with the normal crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
118|mix toggle and no soundtrack-change button.
119|
120|## Playlist mode
121|
122|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
123|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
124|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
125|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
126|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
127|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
128|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
129|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
130|restored selection. The playlist is never persisted, so a reload returns
131|to emotion mode. The style selector stays disabled while it is on, and
132|the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
133|
134|## Similarity and config
135|
136|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
137|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
138|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
139|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
140|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
141|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
142|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
143|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
144|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
145|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
146|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
147|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
148|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
149|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
150|and overrides are unchanged.
151|
152|## Selection scheduler
153|
154|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
155|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
156|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
157|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
158|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
159|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
160|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
161|with the scene it belongs to.
162|
163|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
164|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
165|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
166|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
167|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
168|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
169|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
170|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
171|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
172|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
173|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
174|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
175|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
176|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
177|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
178|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
179|skip override.
180|
181|## Player
182|
183|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
184|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
185|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
186|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
187|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
188|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
189|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
190|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
191|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
192|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
193|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
194|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
195|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
196|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
197|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
198|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
199|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
200|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
201|
202|The bar is one contained row (reader column width, centered with
203|margins): Previous, Play/Pause, Next, the now-playing line
204|(flexible, truncated with an ellipsis), a speaker-icon volume slider with
205|`aria-label` `Volume`, a style selector with `aria-label`
206|`Orchestra / Piano` and no visible label text listing only styles that
207|have tracks (hidden while fewer than two qualify), then
208|`Just play Chopin`. The three transport buttons and the source icon link
209|are icon-only inline SVGs (`currentColor`, 32 px hit area), quiet
210|and neutral, Meta blue on hover and focus-visible, each with `aria-label`
211|and `title` (the source link reads `Source`). Previous walks the session
212|history and restarts the current track with no history, including the
213|current playlist piece in playlist mode; Next cycles same-emotion tracks
214|in the style.
215|A `Just play Chopin` toggle appears only when
216|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; its text comes from the
217|playlist label, it carries `aria-pressed`, and it shows the Meta blue
218|accent while pressed. The now-playing line shows `display title · composer
219|· source`: `displayTitle` drops quoted nicknames, key phrases, and
220|opus/catalogue suffixes from the track title, and the source is the
221|artist plus ` / <platform>` when the attribution names Musopen or
222|Jamendo and the artist does not already say it, dropped when it would
223|repeat the performer. The full manifest title plus the license and full
224|attribution sits in the `title` tooltip. A source icon link stays compact
225|when the manifest provides one. On manifest failure the reader still renders and
226|the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms.
227|Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and
228|keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine, transport, and
229|bar layout; `app/player-controls.tsx` holds the style selector and the
230|playlist toggle; `app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage helper.
231|`core/music-credit.ts` builds the line as a pure function with tests,
232|including the pure `displayTitle`.
233|`core/music-history.ts` is the bounded history stack and
234|`requestManualTrack` in `core/music-schedule.ts` holds a manual pick.
235|
236|## Image api
237|
238|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
239|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
240|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
241|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
242|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
243|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic English message.
244|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Illustrate
245|scene" uses the scene id from the route.
246|
247|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
248|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
249|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
250|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
251|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
252|friendly English message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
253|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
254|
255|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
256|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
257|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
258|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
259|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
260|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
261|and backfills the index.
262|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
263|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
264|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
265|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
266|quota and budget and release the lock.
267|
268|## Chat api
269|
270|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
271|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
272|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
273|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
274|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
275|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
276|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
277|
278|## Quotas and budget
279|
280|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
281|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
282|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
283|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
284|the client, details stay in server logs.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

back afterward.

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on

explain.
